model_interpretation.claim: The supplied baseline is correct on all ten cases and averages 46.67 µs over three samples, but its large-input path repeatedly launches reduction stages and copies the final value. A 256-thread CTA reducing eight coalesced values per thread should produce one partial per 2,048-element tile, using warp shuffles and one block barrier rather than repeated block-wide synchronization. At n=4,194,304 this gives 2,048 partials for a single final CTA; the capped partial count also bounds scratch use for larger positive int sizes. Small inputs fit in one CTA, while n=1 retains a direct copy. Performance remains to be measured by the controller.

items.subject: Large-input hierarchical reduction and warp/block reduction costs
items.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore large-input hierarchical reduction for n=4194304. Replace the current modulo-based interleaved reduction and repeated block-wide synchronization with an efficient warp/block reduction approach, while having CTAs accumulate multiple values per thread from coalesced, disjoint input tiles. Write partials to bounded scratch and reduce them directly to out. Tune tile and block configuration; compare a two-stage path with an additional final reduction stage if the partial count makes a single final CTA inefficient. Cover all legal sizes with bounded reads, exact int32 output, unchanged ABI/default stream, and a correct fallback. Compare all checks and repeated timings against the baseline.
